design_principles.app_approach: The deck is a trial: LSV prosecute (behavioral), FF defend (risk), DT cross-examine (characteristics). Each block gets its own interactive exhibit built from the papers' real numbers.
The Gordon machine returns from Lecture 3: pay up for growth, watch implied g, then watch LSV's Table V verdict that the growth never arrives.

design_principles.principle: The drawdown as a live final exam
design_principles.app_approach: An SR-0.4 patience calculator (Φ(−SR√h)) and a value-spread timeline make the 2017–20 episode the course's most practical lesson.

slides.title: Cheap Beats Expensive — Everywhere You Sort
slides.content_summary: Value vs glamour; the double-sort grids with LSV's real corner returns (C/P×GS: 11.3 vs 21.5; E/P×GS: 11.8 vs 22.4; B/M×GS: 13.2 vs 20.4; E/P×B/M: 11.6 vs 18.9; B/M×C/P: 11.1 vs 19.4). FM regressions confirm C/P and GS carry independent power. The three-way debate is framed.
slides.lux_integration: Lux: 'Why does sorting on BOTH past growth and expected growth widen the spread beyond any one-way sort?'

slides.title: What the Market Is Paying For
slides.content_summary: LSV's design: split PAST growth (realized, averaged-first to survive negative earnings) from EXPECTED growth (Gordon: high P vs fundamentals ⟹ high implied g). Table V verdict: glamour's priced-in growth evaporates by years 3–5 — extrapolation caught in the act.
slides.lux_integration: Lux: 'A low C/P stock could be intangible-rich, genuinely growing, low-risk, or overpriced glamour. How does the past/future split discriminate?'

slides.title: Value Wins When It Counts
slides.content_summary: Figure 2 with the real annual bars: value−glamour positive in ≥17 of 22 years (1968–89) and every 5-year window, including recessions and down-market years. No higher betas or SDs, no bad-state underperformance. Why it survives: limits to arbitrage; data-mining defenses are international and pre-sample evidence.
slides.lux_integration: Lux: 'If value never hurts in bad states, what would FF need to claim to keep calling it a risk premium?'

slides.title: Your Turn: Read the Market's Growth Bet

problem_spec.scenario: Gordon model P=D/(r−g), r=9% for both stocks. Value stock: P=$40, D=$2. Glamour stock: P=$60, D=$1.20.
problem_spec.verification: g = r − D/P. Value: D/P=2/40=5% ⟹ g=9−5=4.0%. Glamour: D/P=1.2/60=2% ⟹ g=9−2=7.0%. The market is betting glamour out-grows value by 3 points forever — the extrapolation LSV showed fails after year 2.

slides.title: The Scoreboard: What Three Factors Absorb
slides.content_summary: The 3-factor model absorbs B/M, E/P, C/P, sales-growth (LSV's own refined sorts: GRS p 0.28/0.39/0.41) and the DeBondt–Thaler reversal (p 0.56) — alphas ≤9bp/mo. The lone rejection: momentum t−12:t−2, GRS 4.45, p=0.000, because losers load like small distressed value and earn the opposite.
slides.lux_integration: Lux: 'Why do momentum LOSERS loading high on s and h make the model fail with the wrong SIGN?'

slides.title: Risk Story, Fine Print Included
slides.content_summary: HML-as-distress; MMV: any three spanning portfolios price identically (single-factor R² 0.79–0.92 → spanned 0.98–0.99). FF's rebuttals of LSV (HML Sharpe unexceptional; premium outlasts the earnings mean-reversion). Data-mining defenses (VW NYSE factors; Davis pre-1962; international; the unification itself). Unfinished: name the state variable.

slides.title: Your Turn: Compute a Fund's Alpha

problem_spec.scenario: A value fund earned 11.2% excess return. Loadings: b=1.0, s=0.3, h=0.5. Premia: market 6%, SMB 2%, HML 4%.
problem_spec.verification: Required = 1.0·6 + 0.3·2 + 0.5·4 = 6+0.6+2.0 = 8.6%. Alpha = 11.2 − 8.6 = 2.6%. Under CAPM the same fund would show α=5.2% — the three factors reclassify value exposure from skill to risk.

slides.title: What Are You Actually Paid For?
slides.content_summary: Covariances (how you co-move) vs characteristics (what you are). Three formal models; Test 1: pre/post-formation SDs barely change — the comovement predates distress (industry/region), killing model 1. Note whose theory is on trial: FF's, not LSV's.

slides.title: Hold the Characteristic, Vary the Loading
slides.content_summary: The clever dependent sort: characteristics first, HML loading within. Risk predicts returns rising with loading; DT's Table III average row: 0.740, 0.817, 0.846, 0.866, 0.806 — flat. The replies: DFF 2000 (disappears over 1927–97), Berk 2001 (dependent sorts biased), DT's answer (dependence is the point). Caveats: EIV favors error-free characteristics mechanically.
slides.lux_integration: Lux: 'Which stocks have precisely estimated betas — and how could estimation error manufacture DT\'s flat line?'

slides.title: Your Turn: What Should Risk Have Delivered?

problem_spec.scenario: Suppose HML carries a premium of 0.40%/month and, within a characteristic group, loading quintiles have h = 0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0. DT's observed average returns across those quintiles: 0.740 and 0.806 %/month at the extremes.
problem_spec.verification: Risk-model predicted Q5−Q1 spread = (2.0−0.0)×0.40 = 0.80%/mo. Observed spread = 0.806−0.740 = 0.066 ≈ 0.07%/mo — one-twelfth of the prediction. Characteristics win (in this sample).

slides.title: The Arithmetic of Patience
slides.content_summary: 2017–20: the deepest value drawdown in ~100 years (every measure ≈−50%). But at SR=0.4 a strategy underperforms cash Φ(−SR√h): ≈34% of years, ≈10% of decades — long droughts are statistically ordinary. Interactive: slide SR and horizon.
slides.lux_integration: Lux: 'At what Sharpe would a 10-year drought fall below a 1-in-20 event?' (SR·√10 = 1.645 ⟹ SR ≈ 0.52)

slides.title: The Suspects — and the Spread
slides.content_summary: AQR's elimination: not FANGs (drop biggest 10% — spread unchanged), not intangibles, not fundamentals, not recessions, rates only 15–30%. What's left: re-pricing. The value spread hit the 99th percentile in 2020 — beyond the tech bubble — implying an 80–110% five-year growth gap no data ever delivered. Post-2000 recoveries ran +75–108%; this one began Nov 2020.
slides.lux_integration: Lux: 'Why does a WIDENING spread mechanically equal a drawdown for a value investor?'

slides.title: Your Turn: How Ordinary Was the Drought?

problem_spec.scenario: A premium has Sharpe ratio 0.4 (annual). Assume normal returns, so P(underperform cash over h years) = Φ(−SR·√h).

slides.title: Same Trade, Two Stories
slides.content_summary: The live test under-determines the why: re-pricing + spread predictability + the 1999 echo lean behavioral; a decade-long negative draw and a time-varying price of risk fit FF. DFA sells the risk story, LSV Asset Management the mistake story — portfolios ≈0.98 correlated. The story decides whether clients survive the bottom; the spread is the instrument both camps watch.
